blocks.value: Inheritance lets you define a new class by building on an existing one. The new class is called the derived class (also known as a subclass, child class, or descendant class), and the class it's built on is the base class (also called a superclass, parent class, or ancestor class).

public class DerivedClass extends BaseClass { }

public class Student extends Person { }
Here, Student is the derived class and Person is the base class. Student automatically inherits Person's declared instance variables and public methods, but not its constructors.
If a derived class defines a method with the same name, parameter list, and return type as one in the base class, that method is said to override the base class's version.
